react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on a single dominant biological signal: tryptophan metabolism is massively perturbed in the treatment group, with an overwhelming fold-enrichment (~750–1351) and FDR as low as 3.4×10⁻¹⁵ across RaMP multi-database ORA, p=0.0029 in the m/z-network mummichog framework, and p=5.41×10⁻⁹ in the KEGG-specific MetaboAnalystR PSEA. The cross-paradigm winner is KEGG:hsa00380 (Tryptophan metabolism), also captured as WP:WP465 (Tryptophan metabolism, WikiPathways) and MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism (mummichog empirical network). Within Reactome, the sub-pathway R-HSA-209931 (Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis) is independently enriched (FDR 3.59×10⁻⁸, fold-enrichment 1351). The driver metabolites form a coherent biosynthetic sequence: L-tryptophan → tryptamine → indoleacetaldehyde → serotonin → melatonin, with 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid extending into the kynurenine branch. Serotonin and melatonin are canonical effectors of serotonergic and neuroendocrine signalling; their simultaneous elevation alongside the upstream precursor L-tryptophan indicates coordinated induction of the entire pathway rather than isolated single-metabolite disruption. The remaining metabolites — 4-hydroxyretinoic acid (vitamin A signalling), molybdenum (cofactor), 4-hydroxy-L-glutamic acid, and 3-aminopropionaldehyde — appear as secondary contextual hits that do not replicate across paradigms and are likely pathway-noise rather than primary drivers.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms (RaMP multi-database ORA, mummichog m/z-network, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA) all identified tryptophan metabolism as the dominant affected pathway. The RaMP ORA returned KEGG:map00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) at rank 1 with FDR 3.44×10⁻¹⁵ and fold-enrichment 750.6, hitting six metabolites (tryptamine, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, indol-3-ylacetaldehyde, melatonin, L-tryptophan, serotonin). The same pathway appeared as WP:WP465 (WikiPathways Tryptophan metabolism) at rank 2 with FDR 4.10×10⁻¹⁵. Reactome R-HSA-209931 (Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis) ranked 4th with FDR 3.59×10⁻⁸ and fold-enrichment 1351, containing L-tryptophan, serotonin, and melatonin as hit metabolites. The mummichog empirical network independently returned MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism as the top hit (p=0.0029), confirming the signal via mass-based inference. Driver metabolites are L-tryptophan (upstream entry point, TPH-catalysed hydroxylation to 5-hydroxytryptophan), serotonin (central intermediate, AANAT-catalysed acetylation), and melatonin (downstream product, ASMT-catalysed methylation). These three compounds form a coherent biosynthetic sequence that is simultaneously elevated, indicating coordinated induction of the pathway. Secondary contextual hits (4-hydroxyretinoic acid, molybdenum, 4-hydroxy-L-glutamic acid, 3-aminopropionaldehyde) were detected at lower enrichment and did not replicate across all three paradigms.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms (RaMP multi-database ORA, mummichog m/z-network, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA) all identified tryptophan metabolism as the dominant affected pathway. The RaMP ORA returned KEGG:map00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) at rank 1 with FDR 3.44×10⁻¹⁵ and fold-enrichment 750.6, hitting six metabolites (tryptamine, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, indol-3-ylacetaldehyde, melatonin, L-tryptophan, serotonin). The same pathway appeared as WP:WP465 (WikiPathways Tryptophan metabolism) at rank 2 with FDR 4.10×10⁻¹⁵. Reactome R-HSA-209931 (Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis) ranked 4th with FDR 3.59×10⁻⁸ and fold-enrichment 1351, containing L-tryptophan, serotonin, and melatonin as hit metabolites. The mummichog empirical network independently returned MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism as the top hit (p=0.0029), confirming the signal via mass-based inference. Driver metabolites are L-tryptophan (upstream entry point, TPH-catalysed hydroxylation to 5-hydroxytryptophan), serotonin (central intermediate, AANAT-catalysed acetylation), and melatonin (downstream product, ASMT-catalysed methylation). These three compounds form a coherent biosynthetic sequence that is simultaneously elevated, indicating coordinated induction of the pathway. Secondary contextual hits (4-hydroxyretinoic acid, molybdenum, 4-hydroxy-L-glutamic acid, 3-aminopropionaldehyde) were detected at lower enrichment and did not replicate across all three paradigms.
